 BREAKING NEWS Updated 15 minutes ago Justice Department Justice Department Virginia State Senator L. Louise Lucas charged in public corruption case
 The 82-year-old surrendered to authorities to face charges Thursday, the Justice Department said. She was charged along with a half-dozen others. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Virginia State Sen. Louise Lucas in February in Richmond, Va. Ryan M. Kelly / AP Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 22, 2026, 9:49 AM EDT  /  Updated   Oct. 22, 2026, 9:56 AM EDT By Ryan J. Reilly and Gary Grumbach Federal authorities on Thursday charged a prominent Virginia Democrat with racketeering and a money laundering conspiracy as part of an alleged public corruption case involving a cannabis business she co-owns. 
 Virginia State Senator L. Louise Lucas, a frequent critic of President Donald Trump who is one of the most powerful Democrats in the state, surrendered to authorities Thursday, the Justice Department spokesperson said. She was also charged with conspiracy to distribute marijuana. A half-dozen others were also in custody also charged in the alleged scheme. 
 The investigation into the 82-year-old Lucas predates the Trump administration, NBC News previously reported . But the Justice Department’s move, just 12 days before a midterm election, is unusual, as federal authorities have typically avoided taking overt investigative steps against political figures so close to an election. Lucas is not up for reelection this year, but has ties to prominent Democrats who are on the ballot.
 NBC News has reached out to Senator Lucas’ office, her legal counsel, and Democratic Gov. Abigail Spanberger for comment. 
 Attorney General Todd Blanche and FBI Director Kash Patel were expected to hold a press conference about the arrest in Norfolk, Virginia.
 In May, federal agents searched Lucas’ office in Portsmouth , along with a business she co-owns called The Cannabis Outlet, which is located on High Street. Virginia Democratic Rep. Suhas Subramanyam said his communications with Lucas were monitored , and said the Justice Department had become Trump’s “own personal law firm, with his former personal attorney carrying out vendettas on Trump’s political enemies.”
 A reporter with WAVY, an NBC affiliate, also received a notification letter showing that his communications with Lucas’ number had been swept up in the wire. 
 The indictment alleges that members of the conspiracy “used various business entities” to “disguise the proceeds of illegal marijuana distribution,” and that Lucas “used her political position in the Virginia state senate to insulate” the enterprise “from criminal scrutiny, to further the goal of wealth accumulation.” 
 In one intercepted phone call in February 2026 with an unindicted co-conspirator, Lucas allegedly said that this was their “last chance at generational wealth,” adding “I’ve gotten too old to not be greedy.”

 Slide 1 of 1 Lucas has been a proponent of marijuana legalization in Virginia. The state now allows for possession of marijuana for adults over 21, but recreational marijuana sales remain unlawful. 
 That is set to change; this summer, the governor and state legislators announced an agreement to allow the licensed retail sale of marijuana beginning July 1, 2027.
 Lucas’ political career began more than four decades ago, when she was elected to the Portsmouth City Council. She was elected to the Virginia state assembly in 1991. 
 The Virginia Senate consists of 40 members who serve four year terms and receive an annual salary of $18,000, a figure set in 1988. Members also receive mileage reimbursement and a per diem during the General assembly session.
 The Justice Department has brought several controversial cases against Trump’s political targets in Trump’s second term. Three weeks before the midterms, federal officials searched the home of Democratic Rep. Ilhan Ohmar of Minnesota in an immigration-related investigation and seized her phone. She has said she will not be silenced. 
 The office of Jeanine Pirro, the former judge and Fox News host Trump named as the top federal prosecutor in the nation’s capital, a ttempted to indict six sitting members of Congress over a social media video that Trump disliked. A criminal case against former FBI Director James Comey over an Instagram photo of seashells remains ongoing .
